title: Smartphones and decision thoughtfulness
description: A research figure redrawn on the light register, 4:3, over a photo of a hand tapping a phone that fades into the ground towards the left: the hook “Why shoppers browse on their phone but buy on a PC” as the title, then device associations (smaller screen size, low work-relatedness) and behavioral associations (portability, rapid interaction design, through micro-moment usage) lowering perceived decision thoughtfulness on a smartphone, as Phosphor icons and labels straight on the ground (the outcome alone in a red box) joined by orthogonal arrows, each sign in a red pill on its arrow. Source: Yuen, Townsend and Tsiros, When and Why Consumers Avoid Purchase on Smartphones, Journal of Marketing (forthcoming).
source: Vincentia Yuen, Claudia Townsend and Michael Tsiros, When and Why Consumers Avoid Purchase on Smartphones, Journal of Marketing (Sage), accepted manuscript, https://journals.sagepub.com/toc/JMX/0/ja: Figure 1, Antecedents to Lower Perceived Decision Thoughtfulness on a Smartphone (vs. PC). Redrawn from the brief's screenshot of it (Nov 2026), wording and signs as given. Icons: Phosphor (MIT), regular weight. Background photo: from the brief (Nov 2026), assets/background.jpg (1470×980).
